subject: Usage mix and pricing — model premium ladder / per-token & embeddings split
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan@acmeai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@procurement.acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Inquiry: 1B token/month — how to structure pricing for mixed chat + embeddings

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: Acme is planning a pilot that could scale toward ~1B tokens/month across Feb–Jun. The mix will be roughly 70% chat (conversational prompts + assistant), 30% embeddings for semantic search. We expect a small percentage (~10%) of that chat volume to hit a premium model (we're evaluating quality on a small set of prompts).

Questions we need answered to align procurement and finance:
- Do you price chat and embeddings off the same per-token ladder or do embeddings get a separate flat per-embedding unit?
- For premium models, do you apply a fixed multiplier on the committed discount or an absolute per-token surcharge?
- How do you handle month-over-month spikes above the commit? Overage pricing vs pre-bought credits vs burst pool?
- Will you provide a blended effective rate (weighted by model mix) for quoting to finance?

Can you send a quick sketch of tiered commit options and an example blended invoice for 1B tokens with 10% premium model usage + 30% embeddings (assume 1 embedding call ~ 1k tokens equivalent for the math).

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Platform, Acme AI
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inquiry: 1B token/month — how to structure pricing for mixed chat + embeddings

Jordan — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. High-level answers up front, details below and I've attached an initial pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx for illustration.

High-level:
- Embeddings are priced separately from chat (per-embedding unit), not off the per-token chat ladder. We provide a dedicated embeddings band because memory/throughput characteristics differ.
- Premium models are handled as a model multiplier on the unit price rather than a fixed per-token surcharge. This keeps discounts predictable across tiers.
- For spikes above commit we offer three options: automatic burst pool (limited capacity, higher overage rate), pre-bought credits that lock in the blended rate, or pay-as-you-go overage (higher than committed tier).
- We can produce a blended effective rate for any hypothetical mix; see the spreadsheet.

A couple of clarifying questions so our numbers map to your finance needs:
1) When you say 1B tokens/month, is that token-count after truncation/response (what you expect on invoice) or upstream prompts only?
2) Is the 30% embeddings measured by call-count or by equivalent tokens? You noted 1 embedding ~1k token equivalent — confirm if that mapping is acceptable.

Next steps: Marissa will outline a recommended commit ladder (3 options) and show the blended invoice example. If procurement wants legal or a term sheet, we can attach redwood-pricing-terms.pdf and a standard SOW.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inquiry: 1B token/month — proposal options attached

Jordan — putting three pragmatic commit options on the table (see pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx attached):

Option A — Conservative pilot (3-month commit):
- Commit: 250M tokens/month
- Chat discount off list: 15%
- Premium model multiplier: 1.35x on the post-discount unit price for chat
- Embeddings: flat $0.80 per 1k-embedding units
- Overage: pay-as-you-go at list price (no burst pool)

Option B — Growth (recommended for predictable budgeting):
- Commit: 500M tokens/month
- Chat discount: 25%
- Premium multiplier: 1.25x
- Embeddings: $0.60 per 1k units
- Overage: burst pool available (monthly true-up) at 1.15x committed blended rate

Option C — Aggressive (best unit economics):
- Commit: 1B tokens/month
- Chat discount: 35%
- Premium multiplier: 1.15x
- Embeddings: $0.45 per 1k units
- Overage: pre-bought credits available at committed blended rate, burst pool at 1.10x

Notes on blended invoicing and how we calculate: we compute an effective per-token rate for chat as: (list_unit * (1 - discount)) * weighted_model_multiplier. Embeddings are billed separately as per-embedding units and shown as a separate line item on invoice.

Example blended math (Option C assumptions):
- Chat tokens: 700M (90% standard, 10% premium)
- Effective chat unit = list_unit * 0.65 * (0.9*1.0 + 0.1*1.15) => illustrates the small uplift from premium mix
- Embeddings: 300M tokens equivalent => 300k embedding units => embeddings line at $0.45 * 300k = $135k

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (row-level examples), redwood-pricing-terms.pdf (standard terms). HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4321

If you want, we can show a few sample invoices (one for each option) and a one-page appendix that maps engineering metrics (req/sec, average latency) to the pricing bands.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Evelyn — thanks for the clear options. Procurement has two follow-ups before we can circulate to finance:

1) For EU-hosted traffic (our main region), can you confirm that the embeddings unit pricing and premium multipliers are identical vs US? Any region surcharge?
2) For month-to-month variability: our traffic can swing +40% during product launches. Which option gives us the most predictable cost exposure?
3) Legal wants to see whether the premium multiplier is applied before or after the committed discount (your email implies after — please confirm for contract language).

We reviewed the spreadsheet and would like a worked example for Option B with 40% spike in month 2 and the resulting invoice lines (chat standard, chat premium, embeddings, overage). Also include a suggested term: a 6-month rolling true-up with a 30-day notice window for the burst pool.

Procurement contact: procurement@procurement.acmeai.com

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan / team — quick answers and next steps below.

1) Region parity: We price list units identically across regions for chat; embeddings list unit parity is the same as well. We do sometimes have a small regional compliance premium for on-prem / air-gapped installs, but for EU-hosted cloud regions there is no region surcharge in our standard terms.

2) Predictable exposure: Option B with burst pool provides the best tradeoff for you: committed discount protects baseline spend, the burst pool covers predictable launches at 1.15x committed blended rate, and the monthly true-up smooths spikes. Option C gives the best unit economics but requires a 1B commit which may be over-provisioned for your team.

3) Multiplier semantics for contract language: multiplier applies on top of the post-discount unit price. Contract clause (draft): "PremiumModelRate = BaseUnitPrice * (1 - CommitDiscount) * ModelMultiplier; Invoices will show discount and model multiplier math on each chat line item."

Requested deliverable: we'll produce a worked Option B example with a month 2 +40% spike and the invoice lines (breakout by standard chat, premium chat, embeddings, overage/burst). Marissa will attach the example and we will add a 6-month rolling true-up clause with 30-day notice for the burst pool.

I'll follow up by EOD with the worked example and a suggested term summary for procurement to review.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
